obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach of student information, including student portal account takeovers, or compromise of the college's SAIG or Department system access
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach; do not wait for forensic confirmation
notify: FSA (Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form and CPSSAIG@ed.gov)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Title IV participant with a SAIG Enrollment Agreement

obligation: FTC notification event (Safeguards Rule)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving at least 500 consumers. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise; data counts as unencrypted if the key was also accessed
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov. Content: name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any law enforcement delay determination (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers (the college holds customer information on about 41,000)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the person committing the breach (314.4(j)(2))

obligation: FTC notice: law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still due within 30 days of discovery and must include the determination and a contact; law enforcement may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: FTC (inside the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if law enforcement asks

obligation: Referral of applicant fraud to the Office of Inspector General
trigger: Credible information that an applicant for Title IV aid may have engaged in fraud or other criminal misconduct in connection with the application (for example, use of false identities)
deadline: The rule sets no fixed number of days; college standard: refer within 10 business days of the credible-information determination
notify: U.S. Department of Education Office of Inspector General
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination that the information is credible

obligation: Referral of employee, servicer, or agent fraud to the Office of Inspector General
trigger: Credible information that an employee, third-party servicer, or agent involved in Title IV administration may have engaged in fraud or other illegal conduct involving the programs
deadline: The rule sets no fixed number of days; college standard: refer within 10 business days
notify: U.S. Department of Education Office of Inspector General
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination that the information is credible
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with General Counsel

obligation: Pay Title IV credit balances to the student (diverted refunds)
trigger: A credit balance refund was paid to an attacker's account, so the student has not been paid
deadline: The credit balance must be paid to the student or parent as soon as possible and no later than 14 days after it occurred (or after the first day of class)
notify: Affected student or parent (payment)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: When the credit balance occurred (not when the fraud was found)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents: first name or initial and last name with an SSN, a government ID number, a financial account or card number with its access code, medical or health insurance information, biometric data, or geolocation information (501.171(1)(g)1.a.); or a user name or email address with a password or security question and answer that would permit access to an online account. Encrypted data is excluded unless the key was also taken
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Up to 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)). Law enforcement may delay notice by written request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Each affected Florida resident (students, former students, parent borrowers) by mail or email; content per 501.171(4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The college's federal rules (FTC Safeguards Rule, FERPA) do not require notice to individuals, so the deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) is not available; counsel to confirm
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the college reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only on counsel's advice; unlikely when SSNs, ISIR data, or bank details were taken

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); content per 501.171(3)(b), including a copy of the individual notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the college (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by the third-party servicer, a SaaS vendor, or another third-party agent
deadline: Agent must notify the college no later than 10 days after determining the breach; amended contracts require 72 hours (POAM-003, POAM-020)
notify: The college (Information Security Manager and Chief Compliance Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts; the college still owes the notices above

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected online students and former students living in any of the 41 states where the college enrolls students, or elsewhere
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); some states also require regulator notice
notify: Residents and regulators under the law of each state where affected individuals reside
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - counsel checks the affected list by state of residence

obligation: FERPA record of the unauthorized disclosure
trigger: PII from education records disclosed without authorization (including through account takeover)
deadline: Record in each affected student's disclosure record, kept as long as the education record is kept. FERPA itself has no breach notification requirement
notify: Internal: the Registrar records the parties (if known) and the incident; students may inspect the record
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Qualified Individual report to the board
trigger: Any security event or violation and management's response
deadline: In the next written report (each October); the board chair and the audit committee chair are also told within 24 hours of a severity 1 incident under POL-03
notify: Board of directors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Clery emergency notification
trigger: An incident creates a significant emergency or dangerous situation involving an immediate threat to the health or safety of students or employees on campus (for example, doors unlocked or cameras disabled during an active threat)
deadline: Without delay upon confirmation, unless notifying would compromise efforts to assist a victim or contain the emergency
notify: Campus community through the emergency notification service (break-glass path if SSO is down)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the incident creates such an emergency

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Report to law enforcement (voluntary)
citation: Voluntary; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) treats timely reporting as a mitigating factor
trigger: Ransomware, extortion, or organized fraud
deadline: As soon as practicable (runbook target: within 2 days)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed rule would cover every Title IV institution regardless of size (N61-R06); recheck when final

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident or fraud loss
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging incident response vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($5 million limit, $150,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Employer partner notice
trigger: Security incident affecting sponsored students' data or the partner portal
deadline: Per agreements: within 72 hours of confirming an incident affecting partner data
notify: The 9 employer partners' designated contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
owner: Director of Corporate Partnerships through counsel

obligation: Lender and PE sponsor notice
trigger: Material incident
deadline: Per credit agreement; sponsor operating partner informed within 24 hours (internal rule)
notify: Lender agent; PE sponsor operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the credit agreement

obligation: HIPAA breach notification
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: n/a
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - the college is not a HIPAA covered entity; counseling and student health records are FERPA-covered or treatment records excluded from PHI (45 CFR 160.103)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the college holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the college holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
